title: Which of these spaces are complete?

prereqs.why: Completeness is the property being tested, and refuting it means producing one Cauchy sequence with nowhere to go.
Three of the five are subspaces of a complete space, where completeness and closedness are the same question.
The last two are the same set of functions under two different metrics, and only one of them is complete.

statement:
Select every space below that is **complete** — every Cauchy sequence in
it converges to a point of it.

Refuting completeness means producing a single Cauchy sequence whose only
possible limit lies outside the space.
hints: For a subspace of $\R$, completeness and being closed in $\R$ are the same condition. Which of these subsets of $\R$ are closed?
In the discrete metric a Cauchy sequence must be eventually constant. What does that make the space?
For the last one, look for a sequence of continuous functions whose integral distances shrink but whose natural limit has a jump in it.
